summary: This RFC specifies the Password Generator service, which returns six random eight-character words with reasonable pronounceability, using a multi-level algorithm. Hosts that choose to offer such a service are expected to follow it.

plainLanguage.summary: A machine invents six made-up words that are easy to say, so you can pick one as a password.

how to generate pronounceable passwords over the network
how many words does pwdgen generate
subtitle: A network service that generates random, pronounceable passwords for users to choose from.

tldr.problem: User-selected passwords are too easy to guess, making systems vulnerable to attacks.
tldr.mechanism: PWDGEN offers a service that generates six random, eight-character words with reasonable pronounceability, letting users select one from the list or request another set.
tldr.outcome: Users can adopt stronger passwords more easily than remembering random strings, but the service depends on good randomness for uniqueness.

today: RFC 972 is an Internet Standard that was never widely deployed. Modern systems use different approaches to password generation, such as passphrase generation or stronger randomization algorithms.

sections.title: The Problem with User-Selected Passwords
sections.content: Most systems let users pick their own passwords, but people tend to choose words they can remember easily, like their name or a common word. These passwords are too easy for attackers to guess. Some sites have blocked common dictionary words, but that leaves users stuck choosing random strings they cannot remember. PWDGEN solves this by generating passwords that are both hard to guess and easy to remember.
sections.plainLanguage: People pick bad passwords because they pick things they can remember. A computer can invent words that are hard to guess but still easy to remember.

sections.title: How PWDGEN Works
sections.content: The service uses a multi-level algorithm to generate six random, eight-character pronounceable words. The key to good results is a strong source of randomness. The RFC emphasizes that seed values should be stored as values greater than 32 bits, and seeds based on a time-of-day clock are not acceptable because they are predictable.
sections.plainLanguage: The computer uses special math rules to invent words. The trick is using really random numbers so it does not repeat the same words.

sections.title: TCP and UDP Variants
sections.content: Two versions of the service are defined. The TCP variant listens on port 129, accepts a connection, sends back the six words, and closes the connection. The UDP variant listens on port 129 for datagrams and sends back the words in a reply datagram. Both services are stateless and simple for clients and servers to implement.
sections.plainLanguage: The service works two ways: you can connect like a phone call, or you can send a message and get an answer back, like postcards.
